title: 고3 레벨테스트 B형
description: 중급~고급: 수능 어휘((A)/(B) 고르기·영영풀이·쓰임 판단), 지시대명사 those·보어 도치·Were it not for·완료 동명사·Hardly had 도치·수 일치, 선택의 역설 글(요지·빈칸)·도시 열섬 글(문장 삽입·주제) 읽기, 배열·영작

passages.title: Too Many Choices
passages.text:
We tend to assume that more choice always makes people happier.
Yet studies suggest otherwise.
In one well-known experiment, shoppers who saw a table with 24 kinds of jam were less likely to buy any than those who saw only six.
When faced with too many options, people worry about missing the best one, and the effort of comparing them becomes exhausting.
Even after making a choice, they are more likely to regret it.
In this sense, an abundance of options can ____________.

passages.title: Urban Heat Islands
passages.text: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. ( ① ) This is known as the urban heat island effect. ( ② ) Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and slowly release the heat at night. ( ③ ) In addition, there are fewer trees in cities to provide shade and cool the air through evaporation. ( ④ ) As a result, planting trees and creating green roofs are now seen as effective ways to cool cities down.

items.explanation: abundance = 풍부함, 많음 (부족함 shortage·lack)
exhausting = 진을 빼는 (사람이 지친 상태는 exhausted)

items.stimulus: Dark surfaces ____ more heat than light-colored ones, so they get hotter in the sun.
items.explanation: 햇볕 아래에서 더 뜨거워진다 → 열을 더 많이 흡수한다(absorb). reflect(반사하다)는 반대.

items.prompt: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르세요.
items.stimulus: Too many options can (A) [enhance / undermine] satisfaction, because people tend to (B) [regret / celebrate] their choices afterward.
items.explanation: (A) 선택지가 너무 많으면 만족을 떨어뜨린다(undermine) (B) 사람들이 나중에 자기 선택을 후회하기(regret) 때문에

items.stimulus: to make someone unable to act, move, or decide
items.explanation: 행동하거나 결정하지 못하게 만들다 = paralyze(마비시키다) (motivate 동기를 주다, liberate 해방하다, persuade 설득하다)

items.prompt: 문맥상 단어의 쓰임이 어색한 문장을 고르세요.
choices: His remarks were irrelevant to the topic.
The evidence was so ambiguous that everyone agreed on its meaning.
The species is vulnerable to climate change.
The treaty was signed to promote cooperation.
items.explanation: 증거가 너무 모호해서(ambiguous) 모두가 그 의미에 동의했다는 것은 어색하다. → so clear that ~ 또는 no one agreed

items.stimulus: Contrary to popular belief, the study found that the drug had little effect; its benefits had been ____.
items.explanation: 통념과 달리 효과가 거의 없었다 → 그 효능이 과장되어(exaggerated) 왔다.

items.prompt: 문장 속 otherwise의 뜻으로 알맞은 것을 고르세요.
items.stimulus: We tend to assume that more choice makes people happier. Yet studies suggest otherwise.
items.explanation: suggest otherwise = 그와 다르게(반대로) 시사하다. '그렇지 않으면'은 접속부사로 쓰일 때의 뜻이다.

items.stimulus: Shoppers who saw 24 kinds of jam were less likely to buy any than ____ who saw only six.
items.explanation: 앞의 복수 명사 shoppers를 대신하고 관계사절의 꾸밈을 받는 지시대명사 → those who ~(~한 사람들)

items.stimulus: So exhausting ____ the process that many people gave up.
items.explanation: 보어(So exhausting)가 문장 앞에 오면 동사 + 주어로 도치 → was the process. 주어 the process는 단수.

items.stimulus: The heat ____ during the day is slowly released at night.
items.explanation: 열은 '흡수되는' 것 → 과거분사 absorbed가 뒤에서 The heat를 꾸민다. 문장의 동사는 is released.

items.stimulus: Were it not for your help, I ____ the project.
items.explanation: Were it not for ~ = If it were not for ~(~이 없다면, 가정법 과거) → could not + 동사원형

choices: Neither of the plans seems practical.
The professor, along with his students, are attending the conference.
It is essential that every student submit the form.
items.explanation: A along with B는 A에 수를 맞춘다 → The professor(단수) … is attending

items.stimulus: She denied ____ the money from her boss last year.
items.explanation: deny는 동명사를 목적어로 쓴다. 부인한 것보다 훔친 일이 더 이전 → 완료 동명사 having stolen

choices: The number of cars on the road have doubled.
Hardly had I arrived when it began to rain.
I am looking forward to hear from you.
She made her son to study harder.
items.explanation: Hardly had + 주어 + p.p. ~ when … = ~하자마자 …했다. ① has doubled ③ to hearing ④ made her son study

choices: 잼은 여섯 종류일 때 가장 맛있다.
선택지가 너무 많으면 오히려 결정과 만족을 방해할 수 있다.
후회는 더 좋은 결정을 내리게 돕는다.
items.explanation: 통념(선택이 많을수록 행복) → Yet 연구 결과는 다르다: 잼 실험, 비교의 피로, 후회 → 선택지의 풍부함이 해가 될 수 있다

items.prompt: 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르세요.
items.explanation: 많은 선택지 → 구매를 덜 하고, 비교에 지치고, 선택 후에도 후회 → 우리를 자유롭게 하기보다 마비시킬(paralyze rather than free us) 수 있다.

items.prompt: 잼 실험의 결과로 알맞은 것은 무엇인가요?
choices: 24가지를 본 손님이 6가지를 본 손님보다 살 가능성이 낮았다.
items.explanation: 'shoppers who saw … 24 kinds of jam were less likely to buy any than those who saw only six.'

items.prompt: 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 알맞은 곳을 고르세요.
items.stimulus: One major reason lies in the materials used to build cities.
items.explanation: 열섬 현상 소개 → ② 주된 원인 하나는 '도시를 짓는 재료'에 있다 → 콘크리트와 아스팔트(재료)의 열 흡수 → In addition 나무 부족(또 다른 원인)
열섬 현상 정의 → 원인(건축 재료, 나무 부족) → As a result 나무 심기·옥상 녹화

items.prompt: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르세요.
choices: 도시는 주변 시골보다 몇 도 더 따뜻한 경우가 많다.
나무는 그늘을 만들고 증발로 공기를 식힌다.
녹색 지붕은 도시의 기온을 높이는 원인이다.
items.explanation: 녹색 지붕은 도시를 식히는 효과적인 방법(effective ways to cool cities down)으로 소개되었다.

items.prompt: 우리말 뜻에 맞는 영어 단어를 쓰세요.
items.explanation: 후회하다 = regret (regret -ing: ~한 것을 후회하다)

items.prompt: 괄호 안의 말을 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 빈칸에 쓰세요.  (그녀는 그에게 사실을 말하지 않은 것을 후회한다.)
items.stimulus: She regrets ______ him the truth. (not, tell)
accept: She regrets not telling him the truth
She regrets not having told him the truth
items.explanation: regret + 동명사(지난 일을 후회) / 동명사의 부정은 not을 앞에 → not telling (완료형 not having told도 정답)

items.prompt: 주어진 말을 바르게 배열하여 문장을 쓰세요.  (선택지가 많을수록 결정하기가 더 어려워진다.)
items.stimulus: ( the more options / the harder / we have / , it is to decide )
items.answer: The more options we have, the harder it is to decide.
accept: The more options we have the harder it is to decide
items.explanation: the 비교급 + 주어 + 동사, the 비교급 + 주어 + 동사. the more 뒤에 명사(options)가 붙어 함께 앞으로 나온다.

items.prompt: 우리말에 맞게 영어 문장을 쓰세요.  <조건> Were it not for로 시작할 것
items.stimulus: 물이 없다면, 어떤 생물도 살 수 없을 것이다.
items.answer: Were it not for water, no living thing could survive.
accept: Were it not for water no living thing could survive
Were it not for water, no living things could survive
Were it not for water no living things could survive
Were it not for water, no living thing could live
Were it not for water no living thing could live
Were it not for water, no living things could live
Were it not for water no living things could live
Were it not for water, nothing could live
Were it not for water nothing could live
Were it not for water, nothing could survive
Were it not for water nothing could survive
Were it not for water, no creature could survive
Were it not for water, no creature could live
items.explanation: Were it not for ~ = If it were not for ~(~이 없다면, 가정법 과거) → 주어 + could + 동사원형
